records.coverage: Ten crash/error laws: rollback before/mid/after rename, no orphan files or residue, idempotent recovery and a real successful-commit control.

sites.label: LAW CHAOS-PUB-ROLLBACK-BEFORE: a crash before any rename leaves every target at its pre-publication content
LAW CHAOS-PUB-ROLLBACK-MID: a crash PART WAY through the fanout rolls back the targets already renamed — no partial publication survives
LAW CHAOS-PUB-ROLLBACK-AFTER: a crash after every rename but before the journal is marked Committed still rolls back — the JOURNAL decides whether a publication happened, not the filesystem
LAW CHAOS-PUB-NO-ORPHAN-TARGET: a target that did not exist before is absent after recovery, never left half-published
LAW CHAOS-PUB-NO-RESIDUE: recovery leaves no temporary, backup or journal file behind at any crash point
LAW CHAOS-PUB-RECOVERY-IDEMPOTENT: recovering twice is safe, so a crash DURING recovery is not a worse failure than the one it was repairing
